data.title: Novo Nordisk to Launch Wegovy Weight-Loss Pill in Sweden Next Month
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Novo Nordisk will launch its Wegovy weight-loss pill in Sweden on Dec. 24, the Danish drugmaker said Friday.

The once-daily pill first launched in the U.S. in early January and has seen strong uptake among Americans, with the company recently disclosing that sales in the country topped $1.4 billion in the nine months through September.

Further launches have followed, in countries including the U.K., United Arab Emirates, Germany, Mexico, Spain, France and Poland, which together saw $190 million of Wegovy pill sales in the period, with most of that coming in the third quarter.

Novo Nordisk has previously said that it expects the tablet to be available in more than 20 markets in 2027.

"The launch of the Wegovy tablet represents a major step forward for obesity care in Sweden," said Jorgen Kronborg Jungersen, chief executive of Novo Nordisk Sweden. "We see that more people become interested in treatment when a tablet is available as an option."

Prices for the pill will be comparable to the current prices for the injectable version of Wegovy, Novo said.

Swedish pharmacies will set their own retail prices for consumers.

data.title: German unemployment rises more than expected in November
data.description:
Key points:
  • Seasonally adjusted jobless rate remained stable at 6.4%
  • Adjusted number of unemployed remains above the 3 million mark
  • Labour office registers 646,000 job openings in November, 23,000 more than year earlier

By Maria Martinez and Ludwig Burger

The number of unemployed people in Germany rose more than expected on a seasonally adjusted basis in November and was above the politically ‌important 3 million mark, labour office figures showed on Friday.

In seasonally adjusted terms, the jobless figure rose by 9,000 to 3.025 million, while analysts polled by Reuters had predicted an increase of 4,000.

"The labour market remains fragile in the fourth quarter, consistent with weak domestic demand in the third quarter, especially investment," said Claus Vistesen, chief euro zone economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

The seasonally adjusted jobless rate remained stable at 6.4% from October.

"The slight economic recovery has not led to a revival in the labour market in November," said Daniel Terzenbach, a member of the Regional Management Board of the Federal Employment Agency, adding that the trends of recent months were continuing.

The German economy grew by 0.1% in the third quarter, less than initially estimated, data showed on Wednesday.

"There is hardly any sign of an autumn upturn. At best, the German labour market is continuing to move sideways," said Marc Schattenberg, economist at Deutsche Bank Research.

Unadjusted, the total jobless figure fell by 19,000 to 2.936 million, from 2.955 million in October.

The labour office said the decline reflected the end of the autumn seasonal pickup. The unadjusted total has been below the 3 million mark since September.

Although unemployment fell in November, as is usual at this time of year, a slight increase is recorded again once seasonal factors are stripped out, Schattenberg said.

In total, 646,000 job openings were registered with the labour office in November, 23,000 more than a year ago.

data.title: Stocks are poised for a Friday jump - right into a $100 billion wave of automated selling, Goldman Sachs warns
data.description:
By Barbara Kollmeyer

Stocks are pointing higher for Friday, but Goldman is warning that more selling by systemic funds is on the way.

With U.S. stocks poised for blockbuster gains on Friday at the end of a volatile, holiday-shortened week, Goldman Sachs is warning of a massive bout of selling still to come.

"The systematic macro space is still in sell mode. We estimate around $70 billion of global equity sales in the last one week and $100 billion upcoming for the next one week after which point it rounds out and turns into small repurchases in early December in the baseline scenario," Goldman Sachs' trading desk led by Paul Leyzerovich, wrote to clients in a note dated Wednesday.

Systematic funds include trading firms known as commodity trading advisors that track trends in markets using price signals picked up by their models and trading algorithms. Given the wave of selling largely driven by tech stocks since mid-October, those investors continue to follow that trend, holding more bets that U.S. stocks will drop rather than rise, said Leyzerovich and his team.

Where systematic investing funds are sitting when it comes to global equities.

Funds that invest based on volatility swings are also contributing to some selling alongside CTAs, especially given rising price swings, said Goldman. The Cboe Volatility Index VIX, also known as the "fear gauge" for markets as it rises when stocks are falling, hovered at 24 on Friday, from a level above 30 the day before Thanksgiving. It surged to 35.89 last Friday during amid the tech-stock wipeout, and remains above its long-term average of 19 to 20.

"Additional market downside mitigates the early December repurchase but does not lead to continued notable sales in our framework," added Leyzerovich and his team, who said that's partly due to how much selling has already happened and what that would mean for positioning sizes.

"Conversely, a big enough market upside could give any potential December repurchases more of a V-shape," they said.

The week started with a massive tech-led COMP rally, which faded into Wednesday. Strategists warned that the bounce was less indicative of a bottoming to stock selling, but rather mechanical purchases by systematic and leveraged funds that got caught out by the market's swing higher.

On a podcast earlier this week Goldman Sachs' co-head of prime broking insights and analytics, Vincent Lin, said that headed into year-end, hedge funds are more likely in capital-preservation mode than chasing the market. That sentiment has been echoed by others, including closely-followed strategists such as Nomura's Charlie McElligott.

-Barbara Kollmeyer

data.title: Singapore Reportedly In Talks With US To Retain Advanced AI Chip Access As Washington Tightens Export Restrictions
data.description:
Key points:
  • New US rules effective November 19 require licenses for advanced chip shipments to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
  • Nvidia partners SMCI and Dell told buyers in four Southeast Asian countries their orders could not be shipped, the FT reported.
  • Singapore said its investigation into Nvidia customer Megaspeed International remains ongoing.

Singapore is reportedly in talks with the United States to maintain access to advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips after Washington tightened export restrictions, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said Friday.

Speaking at the Asia Future Summit, Gan said Singapore was reviewing its procedures to prevent illicit semiconductor trading and would continue working with US authorities to address their concerns, Bloomberg reported on Friday.

“We have not confirmed it,” Gan said when asked about reports that Nvidia (NVDA) had stopped shipments to Southeast Asia.

He added that the government was engaging businesses to assess the impact of the restrictions and would continue working with Washington to help Singaporean companies maintain access to high-end chips.

US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls

The US Commerce Department introduced new export controls effective November 19, requiring licenses for shipments of covered advanced semiconductors to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Washington identified these countries as posing a higher-than-normal risk of chip diversion.

The rules also restrict shipments of advanced chips to overseas data centers that provide significant computing power remotely to companies headquartered in China and certain other restricted destinations.

The measures include an exemption from the five-country licensing requirement for chips destined for US-headquartered companies, subject to reporting conditions.

Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said last week that he expected the restrictions to affect some of the high-end chip shipments passing through the city-state, Bloomberg reported.

Nvidia Server Shipments Reportedly Halted

The Financial Times reported Thursday that Nvidia manufacturing partners, including Super Micro Computer (SMCI) and Dell Technologies (DELL), had informed buyers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia that their orders could not be shipped.

Singapore's government has not independently confirmed the reported suspension, the report said, citing three people familiar with the matter.

Singapore's Chip Trade Faces Scrutiny

The developments come amid investigations involving Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed International and its former executive Alice Huang.

Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said on November 12 that police had investigated Huang over suspected false declarations involving server purchases but found insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed those offenses.

Authorities issued her a stern warning for knowingly providing inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed and barred her from re-entering Singapore. The ministry said the investigation into Megaspeed remained ongoing and that Huang had not been investigated for espionage.

Singapore has maintained that it does not enforce other countries' unilateral export controls but will take action against companies that breach its own laws through fraud or dishonest practices.

Gan said the government would continue discussions with the U.S. while working with businesses to determine how the latest restrictions affect their operations.

data.title: Sahaj Solar bags ₹389.52 crore solar and BESS project order from Mauritius
data.description:
Renewable energy firm Sahaj Solar Limited has received a letter of award from Mauritius' Central Electricity Board (CEB) for developing two solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) hybrid renewable energy projects, with a combined estimated value of ₹389.52 crore.

The projects, each with a capacity of 10 MW AC, will comprise 17 MW of solar PV capacity and 72 MWh of battery energy storage capacity. The aggregate project value is estimated at $42 million, equivalent to approximately ₹389.52 crore.

The projects will be owned, developed and operated through Sahaj Solar's wholly owned subsidiary, Sahaj Energies Limited, incorporated in Mauritius.

According to the company's regulatory filing, each project is valued at approximately $21 million. The projects will be executed in accordance with the terms of the award and the Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) to be signed following the award.

The projects will have a tenure of 25 years.

The company said the order has been awarded by an international entity and does not involve any interest of the promoter or promoter group in the awarding entity. The contract also does not fall under related-party transactions.

H1 FY27 results

The firm had reported a 42.4% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to ₹158.2 crore in the first half of FY27, compared with ₹111.1 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA rose 37.2% to ₹15.2 crore.

The company's profit after tax stood at ₹4.3 crore. Sahaj Solar attributed the lower profit compared with the year-ago period to higher finance costs of ₹7.8 crore and a moderation in gross margin to 18.1%.

The company reduced its trade receivables by ₹92.4 crore during the half-year and generated operating cash flow of ₹73.8 crore, which was used to repay borrowings. Gross debt declined by around ₹59 crore to ₹116.5 crore, while its debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.82 times from 1.27 times as of March 2026. Its cash balance increased to ₹19.2 crore from ₹10.4 crore.

The company also said its board has approved a further investment of up to ₹25 lakh in its wholly owned Mauritius subsidiary, Sahaj Energies Limited, to support working capital requirements for a solar EPC contract.

data.title: Biotest sells European plasma business to Grifols for €220M
data.description:
Key points:
  • Biotest said on Friday it has sold its European plasma collection business to Grifols Worldwide Operations, a subsidiary of Grifols , for €220M. 
  • Under a 30-year plasma supply agreement, Grifols will supply Biotest with plasma, supporting long-term supply continuity for Biotest’s manufacturing operations.
  • The transaction also includes Biotest’s European plasma supply agreements with third parties, allowing Grifols to optimize plasma sourcing and capture efficiencies in procurement and supply chain management.
  • Biotest’s 47 plasma donation centers will also be integrated into Grifols’ existing European network, bringing the combined network to 97 sites across Germany, Austria, Hungary and the Czech Republic. A single operating model will enable more coordinated management of plasma collection across Europe.
  • The deal value will be settled by offsetting existing debt owed by Biotest to Grifols and is expected to close on 31 December.
  • GRFS is up 2.67% in pre-market trading.

data.title: Belgian minister says offers for 20% stake in Belfius bank are too low
data.description:
Offers the Belgian government has received for a 20% stake in state-owned bank Belfius have been too low, Finance Minister Jan Jambon told parliament.

Jambon said late on Thursday the few offers had "provisionally been deemed insufficient" and that potential buyers had been asked to offer more or the sale might not go ahead.

"If (the sale) cannot be done on favourable terms, nothing obliges us to sell," he said.

Belfius declined to comment.

Belfius was created after the state bought the Belgian banking arm of Franco-Belgian lender Dexia in 2011 for €4 billion ($4.4 billion) following the financial crisis.

The government began the process to try to ​sell a 20% stake in late 2025 as it sought to cut ‌debt ⁠while increasing defence spending.

data.title: UK's Centrica warns jobs at Rough gas facility at risk, Sky News reports
data.description:
Britain's Centrica has warned that hundreds of jobs at its Rough gas storage facility are at risk and claimed that ministers had rejected its proposals to bolster Britain's energy security, Sky News reported on Friday, citing a memo.

The British Gas-owner, which shared plans to cut about 1,300 jobs in July, said it was seeking urgent talks with Prime Minister Andy Burnham, the report added.

Reuters was not able to immediately verify the report.

data.title: X Financial Reports Third Quarter 2026 Unaudited Financial Results
data.description:
SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- X Financial (), a leading Chinese fintech platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. This press release should be read in conjunction with the Company's Report on Form 6-K for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, which has been furnished to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and is available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov and on the Company's investor relations website at http://ir.xiaoyinggroup.com.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

  • Total net revenue in Q3 2026 was RMB771.5 million (US$115.1 million), a decrease of 60.7% year-over-year and 22.4% quarter-over-quarter. The year-over-year decline was mainly attributable to substantially lower loan facilitation volumes, which reduced loan facilitation service revenue and post-origination service revenue, as well as lower financing income.
  • Total loan amount facilitated and originated[1] in Q3 2026 was RMB4.35 billion, down 62.6% quarter-over-quarter and down 87.1% year-over-year.
  • Net loss in Q3 2026 was RMB159.6 million (US$23.8 million), compared with net income of RMB421.2 million a year ago and RMB47.0 million in Q2 2026, primarily reflecting income tax expense of RMB184.6 million and a loss from equity in affiliates, net of tax, of RMB70.9 million, which together exceeded income before income taxes of RMB101.9 million.
  • Delinquency rates for loans 31–60 days past due increased to 2.40% (from 1.73% at the end of Q2 2026 and 1.85% a year ago); loans 91–180 days past due declined to 7.83% (from 9.09% at the end of Q2 2026, though up from 3.52% a year ago). The 31–60 day delinquency rate increased both sequentially and year-over-year, indicating that credit trends deteriorated during the quarter, and the 91–180 day delinquency rate, while lower sequentially, remained materially above the prior-year level. During the quarter, the Company observed an increase in the 31–60 day delinquency rate, which may continue in the near term. The Company believes these trends are consistent with broader industry patterns.

Mr. Kent Li, President of X Financial, commented: "In the third quarter of 2026, we facilitated and originated RMB4.3 billion in loans, a decline of 62.6% from the prior quarter and 87.1% year-over-year. Borrower activity continued to contract, with active borrowers declining to approximately 290,269, down 88.1% from a year ago, while the average loan amount per transaction decreased 5.7% quarter-over-quarter to RMB11,983. The 31–60 day delinquency rate increased to 2.40% from 1.73% in the prior quarter, while the 91–180 day rate eased to 7.83% from 9.09%. The increase in the 31–60 day delinquency rate indicates that credit trends deteriorated during the quarter and may continue in the near term, and both delinquency rates remained above prior-year levels. We believe these trends are consistent with broader industry patterns. We therefore continue to prioritize disciplined underwriting, collection effectiveness, and conservative capital deployment. While the business remains under pressure from lower origination volumes and a challenging credit environment, our focus remains on preserving balance sheet resilience and operating flexibility."

Mr. Frank Fuya Zheng, Chief Financial Officer of X Financial, added: "In the third quarter of 2026, total net revenue was RMB771.5 million, a decrease of 60.7% from the same period last year and 22.4% sequentially. Net loss was RMB159.6 million and non-GAAP adjusted net loss was RMB152.2 million, compared with net income of RMB47.0 million and non-GAAP adjusted net income of RMB165.8 million in the prior quarter. Basic loss per ADS was RMB4.38, and non-GAAP adjusted basic loss per ADS was RMB4.14. Operating margin decreased to 11.8% from 19.6% in the prior quarter and from 18.5% in the same period of 2025. We will continue to manage capital conservatively, maintain cost discipline, and preserve liquidity as we navigate the evolving regulatory and operating environment."

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In evaluating our business, we consider and use non-GAAP measures as supplemental measures to review and assess our operating performance. We present the non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by our management to evaluate our operating performance and formulate business plans. data.title: ECB Leadership Change Has No Material Impact on Euro — Market Talk
data.description: The European Central Bank's leadership change is unlikely to alter the near-term policy outlook and has no material implication for the euro, says Brown Brothers Harriman's Elias Haddad in a note. "The ECB Governing Council is not a one-person show; 21 members have voting rights, including six Executive Board members and 15 governors of the national central banks," the global head of markets strategy says. Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president, while Germany's Markus Brunnermeier is expected to replace Philip Lane as chief economist and France's Laurence Boone is set to take over the ECB's market operations role from Isabel Schnabel. The euro is trading flat against the dollar at $1.0964. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Asia spot prices steady amid tepid demand, continued Hormuz flows
data.description:
By Emily Chow

Asia spot liquefied natural gas prices broadly held steady this week as subdued demand, limited spot buying and continued Middle East flows from the Strait of Hormuz offset colder temperatures in northeast Asia.

The average price for January delivery into northeast Asia (LNG-AS) was estimated at $28.40 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) this week, up from $26.90/mmBtu the previous week.

Exports from Qatar, though still below pre-conflict levels, remain above levels seen in the second and third quarters this year, said Kesher Sumeet, senior analyst at Energy Aspects.

"This supply limits Asia's call on Atlantic cargoes, alongside higher coal burn and fuel switching," he added. "That said, the situation remains fragile, and we expect low European storage buffers and the Qatari shortfall will keep competition for spot cargoes strong through the winter."

A cold November has boosted European gas consumption compared to seasonal averages, leading the inter-basin arbitrage to be firmly closed due to strong European demand, as well as stronger Hormuz flows and tepid Asian demand, said Martin Senior, head of LNG pricing at Argus.

This has caused spot charter rates in the Atlantic Basin to fall to remarkably low levels during what is usually the peak loading window, he added.

Europe's gas market could remain tight throughout 2027 and into next winter if gas storage is depleted heavily this heating season and global LNG supplies remain constrained, an Equinor executive said.

In Europe, S&P Global Commodity Insights assessed its daily Northwest Europe LNG price benchmark for cargoes delivered in December on an ex-ship basis at $27.495/mmBtu on Thursday, a discount of $0.675/mmBtu to the price at the Dutch TTF gas hub.

Spark Commodities assessed it at $27.567/mmBtu, while Argus assessed the January price at $27.465/mmBtu.

"European LNG prices rose over the week as colder weather forecasts and rapidly declining gas inventories tightened the continent's winter outlook," said Aly Blakeway, head of Atlantic LNG at S&P Global Energy.

Gains, however, remained capped by abundant Atlantic Basin LNG supply, recovering Middle Eastern output and subdued Asian demand despite colder temperatures emerging across Japan and China, he added.

In LNG freight, Atlantic rates fell to $16,500 a day, dropping below $20,000 a day this week for the first time since early September, while Pacific rates also declined to $44,250 a day, said Spark Commodities analyst Qasim Afghan.

The US front-month arbitrage to northeast Asia via the Cape of Good Hope and the Nigerian prompt arbitrage also via the Cape, are both pointing firmly to Europe, he added.

data.title: Rheinmetall's New 2030 Targets Look Achievable — Market Talk
data.description: Rheinmetall's lower sales and margin forecasts for 2030 look more attainable for the German defense group, Jefferies analysts write in a research note. The company now expects sales between 33 billion euros and 37 billion euros at the end of the decade, down from prior guidance of about 50 billion euros, including contributions from acquisitions but excluding U.S. order wins. Its operating margin should come in at about 20% compared with a prior forecast of more than 20%. Analysts say they welcome the still ambitious but much more achievable targets that are about 2% below Visible Alpha consensus. Rheinmetall shares trade 3.6% higher at 793.10 euros.
